annotationRationale: The question tests applying a newly defined operation, comparing complex components, and calculating modulus. Ordinary complex multiplication supports the expansion. The supplied references give the same short route, so a second method would add no distinct insight.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Comparing components gives b²=40 and b=2a, hence a²=10. Both possible simultaneous signs give modulus √50=5√2, choice E. The defined operation, choices, and key are consistent.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solution 1 supply the same short component-comparison route, which is retained. No shared-bank method or genuinely distinct beneficial accessible route is omitted.
review.annotationCheck: Evaluating the defined operation, comparing complex components, and finding modulus are appropriately assessed. Ordinary complex multiplication is correctly supporting. The local operation node has no supplied national alignment, which is acceptable.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The custom operation gives a²+b²i, whereas ordinary squaring gives a²−b²+2abi. Real-part equality yields b²=40, justifying division by b in the imaginary-part equation. Thus a=b/2 and a²=10. Both possible signs give modulus 5√2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The LIVE and AoPS Solution 1 credits match the supplied derivation. The explanation independently distinguishes the custom operation from multiplication and makes the nonzero-division condition explicit. Source-informed-original is appropriate, with no official-source claim.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening motivates component comparison. The custom evaluation, use of i²=-1, equality criterion, division condition, and geometric modulus formula are all stated at use.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four IDs fit exactly: math:defined-binary-operation-evaluation for the new rule, cnm_h099 for component equality, cnm_h102 for ordinary squaring, and cnm_h098 for modulus. The assessed/support roles match their use.
